title: Early Popularity and Virality Prediction in Social Media: A Systematic Mapping Study (2015–2025)
content: Early popularity and virality prediction studies differ in what they forecast and what information is available at prediction time. We conducted a systematic mapping study of methods published in 2015–2025 using Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. We mapped 155 studies from bibliographic records and synthesized a purposively selected subset of 58 through structured full-text extraction. Feature-based machine learning is the largest family overall (48/155, 31.0%). Graph neural networks form the largest individual family in 2023–2025 (17/52, 32.7%). These counts describe the distribution of methods in the corpus. Within the full-text subset, fixed temporal observation windows and predictions without observed engagement were recurring settings. The central implication is that methods can only be meaningfully compared when the observation rule, outcome horizon, target, and evaluation protocol are specified. We provide a comparison organized by information available to the predictor and recommendations for benchmark design, transfer evaluation, and assessment of explanations.
